LM Studio has added Z.ai's brand-new GLM-5.3-Flash model to its AI agent platform Bionic, bringing multimodal input, a 1 million token context window, and pricing significantly lower than GLM-5.2. Details below.

LM Studio swiftly integrates GLM-5.3-Flash into Bionic

Since its initial launch in mid-July, LM Studio has continued to expand the models and features available on its Bionic platform. The platform, available for macOS and Windows, is designed for agentic tasks such as coding, research, and handling documents and files.

LM Studio Bionic can use locally run models, or cloud-hosted models on US servers; the latter are protected by a strict zero data retention policy.

Shortly after Bionic's launch, the company added support for Moonshot AI Kimi K3. Today, the company is rolling out cloud support for Z.ai's brand-new GLM-5.3-Flash model, stating that its operating costs are up to 10 times lower than GLM-5.2.

LM Studio's announcement came just hours after the official release of GLM-5.3-Flash. The model had previously attracted considerable attention when it was tested anonymously under the codename "Ox Alpha" on OpenCode and OpenRouter.

GLM-5.3-Flash is a 320 billion parameter mixture-of-experts model, activating 18 billion parameters each time, supporting image and text input, and featuring a 1 million token context window.

On multiple benchmark tests highlighted by Z.ai, its performance leads GLM-5.2, with overall performance broadly on par with frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and DeepSeek.
